transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately, my mind has been feeling so foggy, and I just can't seem to focus or make decisions the way I used to. It's really started to get in the way of my day-to-day life, so I agreed it was time to come in and have someone look into it.

Did this foggy thinking start after a medical illness, head injury, or medication change, or did it come on along with feeling depressed or very anxious? Have you also noticed problems with memory, like forgetting recent conversations or appointments?

No, there wasn't any head injury or medication change, but the fog definitely came on alongside a very heavy, depressed mood and exhaustion after I started caring for my sister. These swings between high-energy periods and feeling foggy and drained have actually been happening on and off for several years. I haven't really forgotten conversations, but the fog makes me feel completely stuck making simple decisions and has caused me to do things like miss bill payments.

When you’re in these depressed, foggy periods, have you ever heard or seen things others don’t, or felt strongly that something was true even when others said it wasn’t? If yes, did those experiences happen only during the depression?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that, even during my worst depressed or foggy periods. I’ve never seen or heard things that weren’t really there, nor have I held any beliefs that others found completely untrue.

During the high-energy periods you mentioned, did you need much less sleep and feel unusually confident or euphoric, talk more than usual, or do risky things like overspending? About how long did those periods usually last?

During those times, I felt incredibly upbeat, wired, and so confident that I felt like the only one who could get things in order, often staying up half the night because of endless energy. I don't recall talking more than usual or doing risky things like overspending, and while these swings have been coming and going for several years, I'm not sure exactly how many days or weeks those high-energy stretches typically lasted.

Thinking about your high-energy periods, what is the longest one lasted without letting up—about 4 days, a week or more, or mostly shorter bursts? During those times, did they ever get severe enough to cause major problems at work or home or lead to hospitalization?

I'm really not sure of the exact duration, whether those periods lasted four days, a week, or longer, just that they would go on for a stretch before I eventually crashed. They never caused major problems or led to hospitalization, as I actually felt highly productive and completely on top of things during those times.

Over the past two years or more, have these ups and downs been present most of the time without a break longer than about two months? Or have there been clear episodes where you felt completely back to normal in between?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact timing or how long the breaks in between lasted over the last couple of years. I just know that these ups and downs have been coming and going for several years now.

During your high-energy periods, did you have at least 4 days in a row of needing much less sleep and feeling unusually energized or confident, or were these milder ups and downs more chronic and continuous over years? Between these mood shifts, did you ever feel completely back to your usual self for 2 months or longer?

These ups and downs have definitely been coming and going for several years now. However, I'm really not sure about the exact number of days those high-energy periods lasted, or if I ever had a clear two-month stretch of feeling completely back to normal in between.

At any point, did your high-energy periods clearly last at least 4 days in a row with much less need for sleep, or were they more of a chronic pattern of milder ups and downs over years without clear episodes? During the stretches between them, did you ever feel completely back to your usual self for 2 months or longer?

I'm really not completely sure about the exact number of days those high-energy periods lasted, or if I had stretches of two months or longer where I felt completely back to my usual self. I just haven't tracked the timing that closely over the years to know for sure.

Between these mood changes, have there been times when you felt completely back to your usual self for 2 months or longer? Or have the milder ups and downs been present most of the time for years without such long symptom-free periods?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact timeline or if I've ever had a full two months of feeling completely normal in between. I just know that these big swings between feeling highly energized and feeling completely drained have been coming and going for several years now.

Between these mood swings, do you ever return fully to your usual self for weeks or months at a time, or do you tend to have some ongoing low mood or low-grade ups and downs most of the time? If you do return to normal, what is the longest stretch that usually lasts?
I'm not entirely sure if I return completely to normal or how long those periods might last. I just know that these big swings have been coming and going for several years now.

During your high-energy times, did other people clearly notice you were acting unusually different from your normal self, even if you felt productive? Or were those periods more like a persistent pattern of milder mood ups and downs that mostly felt like part of your usual temperament?

Yes, others definitely noticed a difference, even though I felt like I was "in my flow" and highly productive. I would snap at people if they slowed me down, and I even boasted to friends that I was the only one who could get things in order. These felt like distinct, intense swings that have come and gone over several years, rather than just my usual temperament.

When those unusually energized periods happened, can you remember whether the change lasted at least 4 days in a row, with clearly less need for sleep each day? Or were they usually shorter than that?

I'm not completely sure about the exact count of days off the top of my head, but those energized periods definitely lasted for a continuous stretch of a few weeks at a time. During those weeks, I would stay up half the night working and still feel completely wired and full of energy the next day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current depressive episode with cognitive fog, impaired decision-making, heavy depressed mood, and exhaustion, in the context of recurrent distinct prior elevated-energy episodes lasting a few weeks with decreased need for sleep, elevated/expansive mood, increased confidence/grandiosity, irritability, and clear change noticed by others. There is no history of psychotic symptoms, hospitalization, or severe functional impairment during the elevated periods, supporting bipolar affective disorder with a current mild to moderate depressive episode rather than mania with psychotic features.
